- Build a complete, playable “Tribes 3D with Quake arena vibes” game in the existing workspace.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained Three.js arena shooter with procedural visuals/audio, Quake-style weapons and movement, jetpack, bots, pickups, and HUD.
- Used locally vendored Three.js and fonts rather than relying on runtime external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game shell, styling, procedural arena and textures, player and bot systems, weapons, effects, audio, HUD, and match orchestration.
- Added first-person viewmodels and game controls, including keyboard/mouse and touch input.
- Ran JavaScript syntax checks and launched a local HTTP server for browser testing.
- Captured and inspected screenshots during development.

### Active
- Validate the latest changes in-browser; later arena, lighting, viewmodel, spawn, and killfeed edits were not rechecked with a final screenshot.
- Confirm controls, combat, bot behavior, and match flow; address any runtime or performance issues found.

- (none)

1. Inspect current changes and run syntax checks on all files under `src/`.
2. Reload the game in the browser, test movement, firing, bots, pickups, pause/restart, and capture/read one latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Fix issues discovered and report how to play and any assumptions.

- `index.html`: Game page and Three.js import map.
- `styles.css`: Menu, HUD, overlays, and responsive styling.
- `src/main.js`: Game setup, match flow, combat, and render loop.
- `src/world.js`: Arena, collisions, pickups, jump pads, and spawns.

- `screenshots/`: Development screenshots; latest may predate the final edits.

- The game was served locally with `python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0` in a tmux session.
